hindi: हे देव सविता, यज्ञ को प्रेरित करो, यज्ञपति को सौभाग्य के लिए प्रेरित करो। दिव्य गन्धर्व, जो संकल्प को शुद्ध करने वाला है, हमारे संकल्प को शुद्ध करे; वाचस्पति हमारे बल को स्वादिष्ट करे। स्वाहा।
english: O god Savitṛ, impel the sacrifice, impel the lord of the sacrifice, for good fortune. May the divine Gandharva, purifier of intent, purify our intent; may Vācaspati make our strength sweet. Svāhā.
notes: Obscure: ketu / keta (rendered 'intent', literally a sign, ray or perception) and bhagāya (taken as 'good fortune'; it could also name Bhaga). Gandharva and Vācaspati are named in the line; no further identity added.

hindi: तुझे, जो दृढ़ता से बैठता है, मनुष्यों में बैठता है, मन में बैठता है, तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; इन्द्र के लिए प्रिय तुझे मैं ग्रहण करता हूँ; यह तेरा आसन है; इन्द्र के लिए अत्यन्त प्रिय तुझे। तुझे, जो जलों में बैठता है, घी में बैठता है, आकाश में बैठता है, तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; इन्द्र के लिए प्रिय तुझे मैं ग्रहण करता हूँ; यह तेरा आसन है; इन्द्र के लिए अत्यन्त प्रिय तुझे। तुझे, जो पृथ्वी पर बैठता है, अन्तरिक्ष में बैठता है, द्युलोक में बैठता है, देवों में बैठता है, स्वर्ग में बैठता है, तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; इन्द्र के लिए प्रिय तुझे मैं ग्रहण करता हूँ; यह तेरा आसन है; इन्द्र के लिए अत्यन्त प्रिय तुझे।
english: You who sit firm, who sit among men, who sit in the mind: you are taken with the upayāma. For Indra I take you, the pleasing one; this is your seat; for Indra, you the most pleasing. You who sit in the waters, who sit in ghee, who sit in the sky: you are taken with the upayāma. For Indra I take you, the pleasing one; this is your seat; for Indra, you the most pleasing. You who sit on the earth, who sit in the air, who sit in the sky, who sit among the gods, who sit in heaven: you are taken with the upayāma. For Indra I take you, the pleasing one; this is your seat; for Indra, you the most pleasing.
notes: Three repeated formulas, each addressed to the offering taken up ('you'). upayāma is kept untranslated (an implement or support; sense uncertain). yoni rendered 'seat' (literally womb). The third line has a doubled space after juṣṭaṃ in the source; kept inside the src of the previous token. Transliteration marks ṷ, ḙ in src are artefacts of accent marks, not variants.

hindi: जलों का रस, जो उच्च बल वाला है, सूर्य में स्थित और एकत्र किया हुआ है; जलों के रस का जो रस है, उस उत्तम को मैं तुम्हारे लिए ग्रहण करता हूँ; तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; इन्द्र के लिए प्रिय तुझे मैं ग्रहण करता हूँ; यह तेरा आसन है; इन्द्र के लिए अत्यन्त प्रिय तुझे।
english: The essence of the waters, of high vigour, being in the sun, gathered together; the essence that is the essence of the waters, that best one of yours I take. You are taken with the upayāma. For Indra I take you, the pleasing one; this is your seat; for Indra, you the most pleasing.

text_flags.why: avagraha missing (asi + indrāya); the Devanagari also lacks it; possible typo of the edition

notes: udvayasam is obscure (literally 'having high vigour/food'); marked uncertain. 'taṃ vo gṛhṇāmi' could also be 'I take that from you'; vaḥ is read as 'of you' (genitive). In the src, 'mṷpayā' contains the ṣ-mark artefact only.

words.gram: pres. part. vi-√i, m. nom. pl.

hindi: हे ग्रहो, जिनकी आहुति बल है, प्रेरित जन के लिए बुद्धि की ओर जाते हुए; तुम उन सब का, जो बस्ती में प्रिय हैं, मैंने अन्न और बल एकत्र कर लिया। तू उपयाम से ग्रहण किया गया है; इन्द्र के लिए प्रिय तुझे मैं ग्रहण करता हूँ; यह तेरा आसन है; इन्द्र के लिए अत्यन्त प्रिय तुझे। तुम दोनों मिलाने वाले हो, मुझे कल्याण से मिलाओ; तुम दोनों अलग करने वाले हो, मुझे पाप से अलग करो।
english: O grahas, whose offerings are strength, going (or enjoying) for the inspired one, a thought. Of those, dear in the settlement, of you, I have gathered food and strength. You are taken with the upayāma. For Indra I take you, the pleasing one; this is your seat; for Indra, you the most pleasing. You two are joiners: join me with the good; you two are separators: separate me from evil.

text_flags.why: the Devanagari has सम्पृचौ (au); the ṷ is a transliteration artefact of the accented au
the Devanagari has विपृचौ (au); the ṷ is a transliteration artefact

notes: The first part (grahā ūrjāhutayo vyanto viprāya matim; teṣāṃ viśipriyāṇāṃ) is obscure: ūrjāhutayaḥ, vyantaḥ and viśipriyāṇām are uncertain, and the syntax between the two halves is unclear, so the first sentence is a literal rendering only. 'grahāḥ' is left as 'grahas'; the line does not explain it. sampṛcau/vipṛcau are duals ('you two').

hindi: तू इन्द्र का वज्र है, बल को जीतने वाला; तेरे द्वारा यह बल को जीते। बल की प्रेरणा में हम वाणी से महान माता अदिति को नाम से पुकारते हैं, जिसमें यह सारा भुवन प्रविष्ट हुआ है; उसमें देव सविता हमारे लिए धर्म को प्रेरित करे।
english: You are Indra's thunderbolt, a winner of strength; by you may this one win strength. Now, in the impulse of strength, we call by name with speech the great mother Aditi, in whom this whole world has entered; in her may the god Savitṛ impel dharma for us.
notes: 'set' is read as an optative or subjunctive of √sā/√san 'may he win', but the form is uncertain. 'yasyām ... tasyām' relates to Aditi. 'dharma' (neuter, 'support, order') is kept as dharma; 'naḥ' could also be read 'our'. Who 'this one' (ayam) is is not stated in the line.

hindi: जलों के भीतर अमृत है, जलों में औषध है; और जलों की स्तुतियों में हे अश्वो, बलवान बनो। हे दिव्य जलो, तुम्हारी जो लहर वेग से बढ़ने वाली, शिखर वाली और बल को जीतने वाली है, उससे यह बल को जीते।
english: Within the waters is immortality, in the waters a remedy; and in the praises of the waters, O horses, become strong ones. O divine waters, the wave of yours that rushes forward, crested, a winner of strength: by that may this one win strength.
notes: 'amṛtam' is rendered 'immortality' (it can also mean the immortal drink). 'pratūrtiḥ' is taken as an adjective of ūrmiḥ. 'vājinaḥ' read as predicate 'strong'.

hindi: वायु या मन, सत्ताईस गन्धर्व; उन्होंने पहले घोड़े को जोड़ा, उन्होंने इसमें वेग रखा।
english: Wind or mind, the twenty-seven Gandharvas: they first yoked the horse; they placed speed in this one.
notes: 'vāto vā mano vā gandharvāḥ saptaviṃśatiḥ' is a nominal phrase; how wind, mind and the twenty-seven Gandharvas relate (identity or alternatives) is not stated, so it is rendered literally. 'dadhuḥ' with 'ā' is taken as 'ā dadhuḥ' (they placed in).

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √yuj, m. nom. sg.

hindi: हे बलवान, जोते जाते हुए तू वायु के समान वेगवान हो; इन्द्र के समान दाहिनी ओर वाला या कुशल होकर शोभा से समृद्ध हो। सब कुछ जानने वाले मरुत तुझे जोतें; त्वष्टा तेरे पैरों में वेग रखे।
english: Be swift as the wind, O strong one, while you are being yoked; be like Indra's right-hand one (or skilful one), and prosper with splendour. May the Maruts, all-knowing, yoke you; may Tvaṣṭṛ place speed in your feet.
notes: dakṣiṇaḥ is ambiguous: 'on the right' or 'skilful'. viśvavedasaḥ: vedas is 'wealth' or 'knowledge'; 'all-knowing' is one reading, 'possessing all' another. 'indrasyeva dakṣiṇaḥ' is kept literal; the line does not say what the comparison refers to.

hindi: हे बलवान, तुझमें जो वेग गुप्त रूप से रखा है, जो बाज में सौंपा गया है और जो वायु में विचरता था, उससे हमारे लिए बलशाली होकर, बल के द्वारा बल को जीतने वाला हो और युद्ध में पार लगाने वाला बन। हे बलवानो, बल को जीतने वालो, बल की ओर दौड़ने को तत्पर होकर बृहस्पति के भाग को सूँघो।
english: The speed that is placed in you, O strong one, in secret, that which is entrusted to the hawk and moved in the wind: by that, O strong one, be strong for us, a winner of strength by strength, and one who brings through in the contest. O strong ones, winners of strength, about to run for strength, smell Bṛhaspati's share.

text_flags.why: possible b/v confusion of the edition (Devanagari वलवान्); the sense 'strong' fits balena that follows

notes: 'te' after yaḥ is taken as 'in you' (locative sense of the genitive/dative te). 'samane' = 'in the contest' (samana). 'pārayiṣṇuḥ' = one who brings across or through. 'guhā' taken as locative 'in secret'.

hindi: मैं देव सविता की प्रेरणा में, सत्य प्रेरणा वाले बृहस्पति के सर्वोच्च स्वर्ग पर चढ़ूँ। मैं देव सविता की प्रेरणा में, सत्य प्रेरणा वाले इन्द्र के सर्वोच्च स्वर्ग पर चढ़ूँ। मैं देव सविता की प्रेरणा में, सत्य प्रेरणा वाले बृहस्पति के सर्वोच्च स्वर्ग पर चढ़ गया। मैं देव सविता की प्रेरणा में, सत्य प्रेरणा वाले इन्द्र के सर्वोच्च स्वर्ग पर चढ़ गया।
english: In the impulse of the god Savitṛ, of Bṛhaspati of true impulse, may I climb the highest heaven. In the impulse of the god Savitṛ, of Indra of true impulse, may I climb the highest heaven. In the impulse of the god Savitṛ, of Bṛhaspati of true impulse, I have climbed the highest heaven. In the impulse of the god Savitṛ, of Indra of true impulse, I have climbed the highest heaven.
notes: Four parallel lines (two optative 'may I climb', two aorist 'I have climbed'). The grammar of 'satyasavasaḥ bṛhaspateḥ' is read as a genitive in apposition: 'of Bṛhaspati, whose impulse is true'; the relation to 'uttamaṃ nākam' (Bṛhaspati's highest heaven) is the most literal reading.

hindi: हे बृहस्पति, बल को जीतो; बृहस्पति के लिए वाणी बोलो; बृहस्पति को बल जिताओ। हे इन्द्र, बल को जीतो; इन्द्र के लिए वाणी बोलो; इन्द्र को बल जिताओ।
english: O Bṛhaspati, win strength; speak speech for Bṛhaspati; make Bṛhaspati win strength. O Indra, win strength; speak speech for Indra; make Indra win strength.
notes: Singular imperatives are addressed to the god; plural imperatives (vadata, jāpayata) to an unnamed group; the line does not say who.

words.gloss: O lords of the forest, trees
O lords of the forest, trees

hindi: यह तुम्हारी वह सच्ची सहमति वाली वाणी हुई, जिससे तुमने बृहस्पति को बल जिताया, जिताया; बृहस्पति, बल; हे वनस्पतियो, अपने को मुक्त करो। यह तुम्हारी वह सच्ची सहमति वाली वाणी हुई, जिससे तुमने इन्द्र को बल जिताया, जिताया; इन्द्र को बल जिताकर हे वनस्पतियो, अपने को मुक्त करो।
english: This is that true agreed speech of yours, by which you made Bṛhaspati win strength, you made him win; Bṛhaspati, strength: O lords of the forest, release yourselves. This is that true agreed speech of yours, by which you made Indra win strength, you made him win; having made Indra win strength, O lords of the forest, release yourselves.
notes: Repetition 'ajījapatājījapata' kept as given (two verb forms). 'vanaspatayaḥ' means lords of the forest, usually trees; the line does not say more. The second 'bṛhaspatiṃ vājam' has no verb in the line (ellipsis of 'you made win' is likely) and is rendered as it stands. 'saṃvāk' = agreed or joint speech.

words.gram: pres. part. mid. √mā, m. nom. pl.

hindi: मैं देव सविता की प्रेरणा में, सत्य प्रेरणा वाले बृहस्पति के, बल को जीतने वाले के, बल को जीतूँ। हे बलवानो, बल को जीतने वालो, मार्गों को थामते हुए, योजनों को मापते हुए लक्ष्य तक जाओ।
english: In the impulse of the god Savitṛ, of Bṛhaspati of true impulse, the winner of strength, may I win strength. O strong ones, winners of strength, covering the roads, measuring out the yojanas, go to the goal.
notes: skabhnuvantaḥ (√skabh 'prop, fix') is obscure here; 'covering' is a tentative sense. kāṣṭhā = goal, post of a race, kept as 'goal'. 'vājajitaḥ' in the first half is read as genitive agreeing with Bṛhaspati's epithet.

hindi: यह वह बलवान जोश में कोड़े की ओर तेज़ी से बढ़ता है, गले में बँधा हुआ, पार्श्व में और मुख में। संकल्प के अनुसार दधिक्रा मार्गों के मोड़ों पर फुर्ती से सरकता हुआ उछलता है। स्वाहा।
english: This strong one hastens to the whip, bound at the neck, at the flank, in the mouth. Dadhikrā, following his purpose, gliding along the bends of the paths, bounding. Svāhā.
notes: Obscure verse: kṣipaṇim (taken as whip or sling), apikakṣe (flank/girth), saṃsaniṣyadat and āpanīphaṇat are all uncertain; the translation is tentative. Dadhikrā is a name given in the line (a steed). The long fourth token fuses several words (pathām aṅkāṃsi anu āpanīphaṇat); the split lists them in this order but uncertain.

hindi: और उसके, जो दौड़ता, वेग से बढ़ता और लालायित है, पीछे वायु पंख की तरह पक्षी के पीछे बहती है। बाज की तरह गति करते हुए दधिक्रावा के घुमाव के चारों ओर, बल के साथ पार जाने वाले के। स्वाहा।
english: And after him, running, hastening, eager, the wind blows as after the wing of a bird. Like a hawk gliding, around the curve of Dadhikrāvan, together with the strength of the one who crosses. Svāhā.

text_flags.why: possible: the Devanagari has द्रुवतः; the root is √dru 'run', so dravataḥ is expected

notes: Obscure verse; the translation is tentative. 'parṇaṃ na veranu vāti' is read as 'blows after like the wing of a bird' (veḥ = of a bird); the sense of aṅkasam and of the second half is uncertain. Dadhikrāvan is a name in the line (a steed). The chunk does not state the grammar of 'sahorjā taritrataḥ'.

words.gram: caus. pres. part. √jambh, m. nom. pl.

hindi: बलवान घोड़े पुकारों में और देवों के यज्ञ में हमारे लिए कल्याणकारी हों; वे मापे हुए वेग वाले और सुन्दर स्तुति वाले हैं। साँप, भेड़िये और राक्षसों को कुचलते हुए वे सदा हमसे दुःखों को दूर रखें।
english: May the strong ones be a blessing for us in the invocations, in the divine rite, of measured running, well-praised. Crushing the serpent, the wolf and the demons, may they always keep afflictions away from us.
notes: 'devatātā' read as locative of devatāti ('in the divine rite' or 'among the gods'). 'svarkāḥ' is uncertain (su-arka: 'good praise' or 'good radiance'). 'sanemi' = from of old or constantly. 'amīvāḥ' = afflictions (no further sense). The subject 'vājinaḥ' is rendered 'strong ones' as no noun is given.

words.gloss: in the winning of the offering, wisdom (uncertain)

hindi: वे हमारे घोड़े, पुकार सुनने वाले, सब बलवान और मापे हुए वेग वाले, हमारी पुकार सुनें; हज़ारों को जीतने वाले, यज्ञ या बुद्धि की प्राप्ति में जीतने की इच्छा रखने वाले, जो युद्धों में महान धन ले आए हैं।
english: May those steeds of ours, hearers of the call, all the strong ones of measured running, hear our call; winners of thousands, eager to win in the winning of the offering (or wisdom), who have carried great wealth in the contests.
notes: medhasātā (medha 'offering, wisdom' + sāti 'winning') and 'maho' (read as 'great', modifying dhanam) are uncertain. The line's nominative plurals are rendered as a list. 'nah arvantaḥ' read 'our steeds'.

hindi: हर युद्ध में, हे बलवानो, हमारी रक्षा करो, धन की प्राप्ति में; हे प्रेरित जनो, अमरो, ऋत को जानने वालो। इस मधुर पेय को पियो और तृप्त होकर आनन्दित हो; सन्तुष्ट होकर देवों के चलने के मार्गों से जाओ।
english: In every contest help us, O strong ones, in the winning of wealth, O inspired ones, O immortals, knowers of ṛta (order). Drink of this sweet drink, gladden yourselves; satisfied, go by the paths travelled by the gods.
notes: 'vājino no' read as vājinaḥ naḥ ('O strong ones, us'). 'ṛta' kept as ṛta ('order'). 'dhaneṣu' = 'in the winning of wealth' (locative plural of dhana, wealth/prize). 'madhvaḥ' read as genitive of madhu ('of this sweet drink').

words.gram: pres. part. mid. ni-√mṛj, m. nom. pl.

hindi: बल की प्रेरणा मेरे पास आए; ये दोनों, द्यावापृथिवी, सर्वरूप वाले, मेरे पास आएँ। पिता और माता दोनों मेरे पास आएँ, और सोम अमरत्व के साथ मेरे पास आए। हे बलवानो, बल को जीतने वालो, बल की ओर दौड़ चुके हुए, अपने को शुद्ध करते हुए बृहस्पति का भाग सूँघो।
english: May the impulse of strength come to me; may these two, heaven and earth, of all forms, come. May father and mother both come to me, and may Soma come to me with immortality. O strong ones, winners of strength, having run for strength, cleansing yourselves, smell Bṛhaspati's share.
notes: 'jagamyādeme' is read as jagamyāt + ā + ime; 'ime dyāvāpṛthivī' ('these two, heaven and earth') takes the verb from the previous clause. 'pitarā mātarā' are dual forms ('the two, father and mother'). 'nimṛjānāḥ' = wiping or cleansing oneself (uncertain object). Third line looks like unit 9's third line.

words.gloss: to the lord of the day

hindi: आपि के लिए स्वाहा; स्वापि के लिए स्वाहा; अपिज के लिए स्वाहा; क्रतु के लिए स्वाहा; वसु के लिए स्वाहा; दिन के स्वामी के लिए स्वाहा; दिन के लिए स्वाहा; मोहित के लिए स्वाहा; मोहित वैनंशिन के लिए स्वाहा; विनंशी आन्त्यायन के लिए स्वाहा; अन्त्य भौवन के लिए स्वाहा; भुवन के स्वामी के लिए स्वाहा; अधिपति के लिए स्वाहा।
english: Svāhā to Āpi; svāhā to Svāpi; svāhā to Apija; svāhā to Kratu; svāhā to Vasu; svāhā to the lord of the day; svāhā to the day, to the bewildered; svāhā to the bewildered Vainaṃśina; svāhā to Vinaṃśin Āntyāyana; svāhā to Antya Bhauvana; svāhā to the lord of the world; svāhā to the sovereign.
notes: A series of svāhā offerings to datives. Whether āpi, svāpi, apija, kratu, vasu, antya and the -ina/-āyana forms are names, titles or common words is not stated, so they are kept as names. 'ahne mugdhāya' may be 'to the day, to the bewildered' (two recipients) or 'to the day-bewildered'; read as two. Whether 'mugdhāya vainaṃśināya' are two recipients or one is uncertain; read as one. Double spaces after svāhā in the source are kept in src.

hindi: जीवन यज्ञ से समर्थ हो; प्राण यज्ञ से समर्थ हो; आँख यज्ञ से समर्थ हो; कान यज्ञ से समर्थ हो; पीठ यज्ञ से समर्थ हो; यज्ञ यज्ञ से समर्थ हो। हम प्रजापति की प्रजा हो गए; हे देवो, हम स्वर्ग पहुँच गए, हम अमर हो गए।
english: May life prosper by the sacrifice; may breath prosper by the sacrifice; may the eye prosper by the sacrifice; may the ear prosper by the sacrifice; may the back prosper by the sacrifice; may the sacrifice prosper by the sacrifice. We have become the offspring of Prajāpati; we have gone to heaven, O gods; we have become immortal.

text_flags.why: the syllable tā is doubled (the Devanagari also has कल्पतातां); the following ᳪ is a stray sandhi sign for the next word śrotram

notes: 'devāḥ' after 'svar' is taken as a vocative ('O gods'); it could be read with the next phrase. 'back' for pṛṣṭha (it can also be a name of a sāman or stoma; the line gives only the plain word). The double space before the last 'yajño' in the source is kept in src.

hindi: हममें तुम्हारा पराक्रम हो, हममें पौरुष और संकल्प हो; हममें तुम्हारे तेज हों। माता पृथ्वी को नमस्कार, माता पृथ्वी को नमस्कार। यह तेरी शासिका है; तू नियन्ता है, संयम करने वाला है, तू दृढ़ है, धारण करने वाला है। तुझे कृषि के लिए, तुझे क्षेम के लिए, तुझे धन के लिए, तुझे पोषण के लिए।
english: Let your vigour be in us, in us manliness and resolve; let your splendours be in us. Homage to the mother Earth, homage to the mother Earth. This is your ruler; you are the controller, the restrainer; you are firm, the supporter. You for cultivation, you for security, you for wealth, you for nourishment.
notes: 'asme' (in us / to us) and the sense of 'vaḥ' (your) are tentative. 'iyaṃ te rāṭ': 'this' is not identified in the line; 'rāṭ' feminine, rendered 'ruler'. 'pṛthivyā iyam' is pṛthivyai + iyam (ai before vowel gives ā). The addressee of 'you' in the last part is not stated.

hindi: बल की प्रेरणा ने पहले इस राजा सोम को ओषधियों में और जलों में उत्पन्न किया। वे हमारे लिए मधुर हों; हम राष्ट्र में पुरोहितों के साथ जागरूक रहें। स्वाहा।
english: The impulse of strength has first brought forth this king Soma, in the plants, in the waters. May they be honeyed for us; may we be wakeful in the kingdom, with priests placed in front. Svāhā.
notes: 'suṣuve' (√sū) could be 'has brought forth/impelled' or 'was pressed'; read as an active sense. 'tāḥ' is taken to refer back to the plants and waters. 'purohitāḥ' ('placed in front', family priests) could modify 'we' or describe the priests themselves.

words.gram: pres. part. pra-√jñā, m. nom. sg.

hindi: बल की प्रेरणा, जो सम्राट् है, इस को, आकाश को और इन सब लोकों को प्राप्त हुई है। जानता हुआ वह न देना चाहने वाले से भी दिलवाता है; वह हमें सब वीरों से युक्त धन प्रदान करे। स्वाहा।
english: The impulse of strength, the sovereign, has resorted to this one, to the sky and to all these worlds. Knowing, he makes the unwilling one give; may he bestow on us wealth rich in all heroes. Svāhā.
notes: 'imām' is a feminine accusative 'this (one)'; the line does not say what it refers to (earth is a likely guess but not stated). 'samrāṭ' is taken with the impulse (sovereign). 'saḥ' (he) is taken as the same sovereign.

words.gram: caus. pres. part., m. nom. sg.

hindi: अब बल की प्रेरणा इन सब लोकों को चारों ओर से घेर चुकी है। राजा सदा से जानता हुआ चारों ओर जाता है और हमारे लिए सन्तान और पुष्टि बढ़ाता है। स्वाहा।
english: Now the impulse of strength has come to encompass all these worlds on every side. The king, knowing, goes round, as of old, increasing for us offspring and prosperity. Svāhā.
notes: 'ā babhūva' taken as 'has come around / encompassed'; 'sanemi' = from of old or continually. 'asme' = for us (or in us). The 'king' is not identified by the line.

hindi: सहायता के लिए हम राजा सोम, अग्नि, आदित्यों, विष्णु, सूर्य, ब्रह्मन् और बृहस्पति को पकड़ते हैं। स्वाहा।
english: For help we lay hold of King Soma and Agni, the Ādityas, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Brahman and Bṛhaspati. Svāhā.
notes: anvārabhāmahe: 'we take hold of / attach ourselves to' (anu-ā-rabh); the verb governs all the accusatives. 'brahmāṇam' is the accusative of brahman and is left as 'Brahman' (it could mean the priest called Brahman; the line does not say). Double space after viṣṇu in source is inside src.

hindi: अर्यमा, बृहस्पति और इन्द्र को देने के लिए प्रेरित करो; वाक्, विष्णु, सरस्वती, सविता और बलवान को भी। स्वाहा।
english: Urge Aryaman, Bṛhaspati and Indra to giving; also Speech, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, Savitṛ and the strong one. Svāhā.
notes: The addressee of 'codaya' is not stated. 'vācam' is the accusative of vāc (speech); whether it is a goddess is not stated by the line, so it is rendered 'Speech'. The second half has no verb of its own; it is read as continuing the objects of 'codaya'. 'vājinam' = 'the strong one' (a steed or personal epithet; not identified).

hindi: हे अग्नि, यहाँ हमारी ओर बोलो; हमारे प्रति सुमन बनो। हमें प्रदान करो, हे हज़ारों को जीतने वाले; क्योंकि तुम धन देने वाले हो। स्वाहा।
english: O Agni, speak here toward us; be kindly disposed toward us. Bestow on us, O winner of thousands, for you are the giver of wealth. Svāhā.
notes: 'acchā vada' is read as 'speak toward (us)'; some take it as 'address' or 'speak to'. 'sahasrajit tvaṃ' = sahasrajit (vocative) + tvam (the source writes sahasrajittvaṃ). The double space before 'hi' in the source is kept in src.

hindi: अर्यमा हमें प्रदान करे, पूषा प्रदान करे, बृहस्पति प्रदान करे; दिव्य वाणी हमें दे। स्वाहा।
english: May Aryaman bestow on us, Pūṣan bestow, Bṛhaspati bestow; may divine Speech give to us. Svāhā.
notes: The object of the bestowing is not stated in the line (the verb is used without object).

hindi: देव सविता की प्रेरणा में, अश्विनों की भुजाओं से, पूषा के हाथों से, सरस्वती के लिए, वाणी के नियन्ता के नियन्त्रण में मैं रखता हूँ। बृहस्पति के साम्राज्य से तुझे अभिषिक्त करता हूँ, अमुक को।
english: In the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the two Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, for Sarasvatī, I place you in the control of the controller of speech; I sprinkle you with the sovereignty of Bṛhaspati, so-and-so.
notes: The first clause is incomplete in itself; 'tvā' of the first line is taken with 'dadhāmi'. 'yantur yantriye': 'in the control (yantriya) of the controller' is tentative. 'asau' is a placeholder for a name ('so-and-so') to be pronounced. 'abhiṣiñcāmi' = 'I sprinkle over' (consecration).

hindi: अग्नि ने एक अक्षर से प्राण को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ। दोनों अश्विनों ने दो अक्षरों से दो पैर वाले मनुष्यों को जीत लिया; मैं उन्हें जीतूँ। विष्णु ने तीन अक्षरों से तीनों लोकों को जीत लिया; मैं उन्हें जीतूँ। सोम ने चार अक्षरों से चार पैर वाले पशुओं को जीत लिया; मैं उन्हें जीतूँ।
english: Agni with one syllable won the breath; may I win it. The two Aśvins with two syllables won the two-footed, the humans; may I win them. Viṣṇu with three syllables won the three worlds; may I win them. Soma with four syllables won the four-footed animals; may I win them.
notes: 'ujjeṣam' (ud-jeṣam) is read as a 1 sg. subjunctive/injunctive 'may I win up'; unit 13 shows the same form 'jeṣam'. Double space after the first line's last token ('ujjeṣaṃᳪ') is not present; the ᳪ is a sign of the following sandhi.

hindi: पूषा ने पाँच अक्षरों से पाँच दिशाओं को जीत लिया; मैं उन्हें जीतूँ। सविता ने छह अक्षरों से छह ऋतुओं को जीत लिया; मैं उन्हें जीतूँ। मरुतों ने सात अक्षरों से सात ग्राम्य पशुओं को जीत लिया; मैं उन्हें जीतूँ। बृहस्पति ने आठ अक्षरों से गायत्री को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ।
english: Pūṣan with five syllables won the five directions; may I win them. Savitṛ with six syllables won the six seasons; may I win them. The Maruts with seven syllables won the seven domestic animals; may I win them. Bṛhaspati with eight syllables won the Gāyatrī; may I win it.
notes: Same pattern as unit 31. 'grāmyān paśūn' = domestic (village) animals; the seven are not listed. 'Gāyatrī' is kept as a name as the line gives no further word.

hindi: मित्र ने नौ अक्षरों से त्रिवृत् स्तोम को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ। वरुण ने दस अक्षरों से विराज् को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ। इन्द्र ने ग्यारह अक्षरों से त्रिष्टुभ् को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ। सब देवों ने बारह अक्षरों से जगती को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ।
english: Mitra with nine syllables won the threefold (trivṛt) stoma; may I win it. Varuṇa with ten syllables won the Virāj; may I win it. Indra with eleven syllables won the Triṣṭubh; may I win it. All the gods with twelve syllables won the Jagatī; may I win it.
notes: Same pattern as units 31-32. Virāj, Triṣṭubh and Jagatī are kept as names; stoma is left untranslated. 'viśve devāḥ' = all the gods.

hindi: वसुओं ने तेरह अक्षरों से त्रयोदश स्तोम को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ। रुद्रों ने चौदह अक्षरों से चतुर्दश स्तोम को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ। आदित्यों ने पन्द्रह अक्षरों से पञ्चदश स्तोम को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ। अदिति ने सोलह अक्षरों से षोडश स्तोम को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ। प्रजापति ने सत्रह अक्षरों से सप्तदश स्तोम को जीत लिया; मैं उसे जीतूँ।
english: The Vasus with thirteen syllables won the thirteenfold stoma; may I win it. The Rudras with fourteen syllables won the fourteenfold stoma; may I win it. The Ādityas with fifteen syllables won the fifteenfold stoma; may I win it. Aditi with sixteen syllables won the sixteenfold stoma; may I win it. Prajāpati with seventeen syllables won the seventeenfold stoma; may I win it.
notes: Same pattern as units 31-33. stoma is left untranslated. The source has double spaces after several 'śaᳪ' tokens (kept inside src of those tokens).

words.gloss: for those sitting on the south
for those led by the Viśvedevas
for those led by Mitra and Varuṇa
for those led by the Maruts
for those sitting on the north

hindi: हे निर्ऋति, यह तेरा भाग है; उसका सेवन कर। स्वाहा। अग्नि को नेता मानने वाले, आगे बैठने वाले देवों के लिए स्वाहा। यम को नेता मानने वाले, दक्षिण में बैठने वाले देवों के लिए स्वाहा। विश्वेदेवों को नेता मानने वाले, पीछे बैठने वाले देवों के लिए स्वाहा। मित्र और वरुण को या मरुतों को नेता मानने वाले, उत्तर में बैठने वाले देवों के लिए स्वाहा। सोम को नेता मानने वाले, ऊपर बैठने वाले, सेवा करने वाले देवों के लिए स्वाहा।
english: This is your share, O Nirṛti; enjoy it. Svāhā. To the gods led by Agni, who sit in front, svāhā. To the gods led by Yama, who sit on the south, svāhā. To the gods led by the Viśvedevas, who sit behind, svāhā. To the gods led by Mitra and Varuṇa, or led by the Maruts, who sit on the north, svāhā. To the gods led by Soma, who sit above, the homage-paying, svāhā.
notes: Obscure: duvasvadbhyaḥ ('paying homage / worshipful', uncertain). 'sadbhyaḥ' is the dative plural of sad ('sitting'); netrebhyaḥ = 'having X as leader'. 'marunnetrebhyaḥ' = marut-netrebhyaḥ with regular nasal sandhi. 'pura̱ḥ sadbhyaḥ' is two tokens in the source (puraḥ, sadbhyaḥ). Double spaces in the source after 'sadbhyaḥ' are inside src.

hindi: जो देव अग्नि को नेता मानने वाले और आगे बैठने वाले हैं, उनके लिए स्वाहा। जो देव यम को नेता मानने वाले और दक्षिण में बैठने वाले हैं, उनके लिए स्वाहा। जो देव विश्वेदेवों को नेता मानने वाले और पीछे बैठने वाले हैं, उनके लिए स्वाहा। जो देव मित्र और वरुण को या मरुतों को नेता मानने वाले और उत्तर में बैठने वाले हैं, उनके लिए स्वाहा। जो देव सोम को नेता मानने वाले, ऊपर बैठने वाले और सेवा करने वाले हैं, उनके लिए स्वाहा।
english: The gods who are led by Agni and sit in front: to them svāhā. The gods who are led by Yama and sit on the south: to them svāhā. The gods who are led by the Viśvedevas and sit behind: to them svāhā. The gods who are led by Mitra and Varuṇa or by the Maruts and sit on the north: to them svāhā. The gods who are led by Soma, who sit above, the homage-paying: to them svāhā.
notes: Parallel to unit 35 with relative clauses. duvasvantaḥ is uncertain ('having homage / worshipful'). 'vottarāsadaḥ' = vā + uttarāsadaḥ. Double spaces in the source after 'svāhā' are inside src.

hindi: हे अग्नि, आक्रमणों पर प्रबल हो; शत्रुओं को दूर फेंककर, कठिनाई से पार किए जाने वाले, शत्रुतापूर्ण शक्तियों को पार करते हुए तेज प्रदान करो, हे यज्ञ को वहन करने वाले।
english: O Agni, prevail over the onsets; having cast off the foes, hard to overcome, overcoming the hostile powers, bestow splendour, O bearer of the sacrifice.
notes: 'abhimātīr apāsya' = abhimātīḥ apa asya (having thrown off the foes). 'dhāḥ' is read as an imperative-injunctive 'bestow'. 'duṣṭaraḥ' (nominative, 'hard to overcome') is read as describing Agni.

hindi: देव सविता की प्रेरणा में, अश्विनों की भुजाओं से और पूषा के हाथों से, उपांशु के वीर्य से मैं आहुति देता हूँ; मारा गया राक्षस। स्वाहा। राक्षसों के वध के लिए हमने तुझे मारा, हमने राक्षस को मारा; वह अमुक मारा गया।
english: In the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the two Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, with the vigour of the upāṃśu I offer: the demon is slain. Svāhā. For the slaying of the demons we have slain you; we have slain the demon; that one, so-and-so, is slain.
notes: 'tvā' as the object of 'abadhiṣma' is odd (we slew 'you' for the slaying of demons); the sense is uncertain, rendered literally. 'upāṃśu' is left as a term (uncertain; literally 'quietly'). 'asau' is a placeholder name ('so-and-so'). 'hatam rakṣaḥ' may be read 'slain is the demon'. The double space after 'hataᳪ' in the source is inside src.

words.gloss: of the lords of the forest

hindi: सविता तुझे प्रेरणाओं के बीच प्रेरित करे, अग्नि गृहपतियों के बीच, सोम वनस्पतियों के बीच। बृहस्पति वाणी के लिए, इन्द्र श्रेष्ठता के लिए, रुद्र पशुओं के लिए, सत्य मित्र, और वरुण धर्मपतियों के बीच प्रेरित करे।
english: May Savitṛ impel you among the impulses, Agni among the householders, Soma among the lords of the forest; Bṛhaspati for speech, Indra for pre-eminence, Rudra for the animals, Mitra the true, Varuṇa among the lords of dharma.
notes: The verb 'suvatām' is stated once and carried through the list (ellipsis). 'savānām' may also mean 'of the pressings'; read 'impulses'. The second line lists gods with case endings that differ (genitives and datives) and no verb; the parallel 'may X impel you' is supplied only as in the first line. 'satyaḥ' is read as an epithet of Mitra. 'vanaspatīnām' = of the lords of the forest, trees.

hindi: हे देवो, इस शत्रुरहित को महान क्षात्र बल के लिए, महान श्रेष्ठता के लिए, महान जनराज्य के लिए और इन्द्र के पराक्रम के लिए प्रेरित करो। इसे, अमुक के पुत्र को, अमुकी के पुत्र को, इस जन के लिए। हे उधर वालो, यह तुम्हारा राजा है; सोम हम ब्राह्मणों का राजा है।
english: O gods, impel this one, without rival, for great ruling power, for great pre-eminence, for great lordship over the people, for the vigour of Indra. This one, the son of so-and-so (m.), the son of so-and-so (f.), for this clan. This is your king, O you yonder; Soma is the king of us brāhmaṇas.
notes: 'amuṣya ... amuṣyai' are placeholders (the father's and mother's names) to be spoken. 'vo'mī' is read vaḥ + amī ('your, you yonder'), uncertain. 'asyai viśe' = for this clan (people). The two sentences of line 2 have no governing verb of their own; 'impel this one ...' of line 1 carries over.
